body.statement:
Consider the singleton-covariate submodel \(\mathcal X=\{x_0\}\) with known rational assignment probabilities \(\bar\pi_z\geq\pi_*\), perfect compliance \(D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=z\), \(s(x_0)=+1\), finite-grid potential wages \(Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)\in\mathcal Y\), observed variables generated by the declared consistency maps, randomized assignment, monotone employment \(S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)\geq S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\), and \(P(EE)\geq m_*>0\), where \(EE=\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}\).  The induced law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\); every unit is a complier, the always-selected-complier event equals \(EE\), and
\[
M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE).
\]
This is an embedding only of that discrete perfect-compliance submodel.  There is no inclusion of the unrestricted Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes class in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and their marginal sharpness conclusion does not automatically transfer outside the stated restriction or to the same-law joint identified set.
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: direct verification of every maintained restriction and equality of principal strata.}

The cited node \(\text{lem:bffl-randomized-always-employed-model}\) records the source model's randomization, employment monotonicity, and always-employed target.  We verify only the stated restricted embedding.  Since \(\mathcal X=\{x_0\}\), \(P(X=x_0)=1\geq\pi_*\).  The declared table has \(\pi_z(x_0)=\bar\pi_z\geq\pi_*\), so the known-assignment and instrument-stratum positivity conditions hold.  Random assignment gives the conditional independence condition because conditioning on the constant \(X\) changes nothing.

Perfect compliance gives, for every unit,
\[
D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1>0=D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0).                                  \tag{45}
\]
Thus the no-defiers restriction holds and every unit is a complier.  Defining \(D=D^{\mathrm{pot}}(Z)\), \(S=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(D)\), and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(D)\) on \(\{S=1\}\), with \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=\dagger\) on \(\{S=0\}\), verifies the three consistency and exclusion conditions equation by equation.  Because \(s(x_0)=+1\), employment monotonicity gives
\[
s(x_0)\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)-S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\}
=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)-S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\geq0,                               \tag{46}
\]
so the complier-conditional selection-monotonicity condition holds.  The finite wage-grid premise gives the declared outcome support.

By (45), the always-selected-complier event is
\[
\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),
S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}=EE.                              \tag{47}
\]
Random assignment, perfect compliance, and the consistency maps reduce the observed contrasts defining \(c_{axk}\) to
\[
c_{0x_0k}=P\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1,Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=y_k\},
\qquad
c_{1x_0k}=P\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1,Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=y_k\}.                 \tag{47a}
\]
Indeed, in each arm the compatible treatment cell has probability \(\bar\pi_z\) times the displayed potential-outcome event, while the cross-treatment cell is empty by perfect compliance; division is valid because \(\bar\pi_z\geq\pi_*>0\).  Summing (47a) over the finite wage grid gives
\[
q_{0x_0}=P\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1\},
\qquad
q_{1x_0}=P\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}.                                         \tag{47b}
\]
Monotone employment implies that the first event is contained in the second.  Consequently
\[
m_{x_0}=\min\{q_{0x_0},q_{1x_0}\}
=P\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1\}=P(EE).                                           \tag{47c}
\]
There is one covariate cell, so summing (47c) over the singleton support gives
\[
M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE)\geq m_*>0.                                             \tag{48}
\]
All nine restrictions in \(\text{def:causal-model}\) have now been checked, proving membership in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\).  Perfect compliance and the singleton support are extra restrictions, so this argument proves only a submodel embedding.  Removing either does not follow from Assumptions A--B or Proposition 1, and nothing in the cited marginal bound constructs a common latent completion for several quantiles; therefore neither unrestricted-class inclusion nor same-law joint sharpness follows.
